title: Steam Measurement
focus: Boiler systems, steam distribution, energy use, vortex flowmeter selection and compensation requirements.

image.alt: Industrial steam pipeline with visible vapor and an installed flowmeter

cardDescription: Boiler systems, steam distribution, energy use and compensation requirements.
whereItFits: Steam lines often change with pressure, temperature and insulation conditions.
siteCondition: Steam lines often operate with changing pressure and temperature, insulation limits and limited straight pipe.
challenge: A quote based only on pipe size can miss the real steam flow range, pressure state and installation limitations.

metadata.title: Industrial Steam Flow Measurement | Velomac
metadata.description: Review steam flow measurement conditions, vortex meter direction, operating details and site information for boiler and steam distribution systems.

detailPage.introduction: Steam meter selection begins with the steam state, real flow range, pressure, temperature and available installation space—not pipe size alone.
detailPage.measurementTitle: Define the steam condition and operating range
detailPage.measurementText: Review the steam type, minimum-to-maximum flow, pressure and temperature together so the measurement direction matches the working line.

title: Gas Flow Measurement
focus: Compressed air, natural gas, industrial gas, thermal mass, gas turbine and vortex options.

image.alt: Industrial gas process pipeline and installed flowmeter

cardDescription: Compressed air, natural gas and industrial gas measurement options.
whereItFits: Gas lines vary by composition, pressure, temperature and output requirements.
siteCondition: Industrial gas systems can vary by gas composition, pressure, flow profile and required output signal.
challenge: Different gas applications may need mass flow, standard volumetric flow, turbine measurement or vortex measurement.

metadata.title: Industrial Gas Flow Measurement Applications | Velomac
metadata.description: Compare industrial gas flow measurement directions for compressed air, natural gas and process gases using actual line and operating conditions.

detailPage.introduction: Gas composition, pressure, temperature, required output and whether mass or volumetric flow is needed all influence the meter direction.
detailPage.measurementTitle: Clarify the gas and required measurement basis
detailPage.measurementText: Prepare the gas type, operating range and pressure-temperature condition before comparing thermal mass, turbine or vortex options.
detailPage.ctaTitle: Discuss a Gas Flow Measurement Application

title: Conductive Liquid Measurement
focus: Water, wastewater, chemical liquids, slurry-compatible conditions and electromagnetic flowmeter selection.

image.alt: Water process pipeline with pumps and installed flowmeter

cardDescription: Water, wastewater and chemical liquids using electromagnetic measurement.
whereItFits: Conductive liquids depend on conductivity, lining, electrode material and grounding.
siteCondition: Conductive liquids require attention to conductivity, lining material, electrodes and installation grounding.
challenge: Material compatibility and low conductivity can affect meter configuration and long-term measurement behavior.

metadata.title: Conductive Liquid Flow Measurement | Velomac
metadata.description: Review electromagnetic flowmeter selection for water, wastewater and conductive chemical liquids using conductivity, material and installation details.

detailPage.introduction: Conductivity, lining and electrode compatibility, grounding and the actual flow range should be reviewed together for conductive liquid service.
detailPage.measurementText: Define the liquid, conductivity, temperature, lining and electrode direction before the electromagnetic meter configuration is selected.

title: Chemical Process Lines
focus: Material compatibility, lining selection, electrode selection and corrosion considerations.

image.alt: Clean stainless steel chemical process line and vessel

cardDescription: Material compatibility, lining selection and corrosion considerations.
whereItFits: Chemical lines need the right lining, electrode material and connection choice.
siteCondition: Chemical lines may include corrosive media, solids, temperature variation and strict material requirements.
challenge: The wrong lining or electrode material can create compatibility issues even when the meter type is correct.

metadata.title: Chemical Process Flow Measurement | Velomac
metadata.description: Review chemical process flow measurement using media concentration, material compatibility, temperature, pressure and connection requirements.

detailPage.introduction: Chemical flow measurement starts with the actual chemical, concentration and wetted-material requirements before a meter family or connection is chosen.
detailPage.measurementTitle: Match the measurement direction to the chemical
detailPage.measurementText: Review corrosion, solids, concentration, pressure and temperature together with lining, electrode and connection requirements.

title: High Vibration Pipelines
focus: Pump areas, compressors, process vibration, signal stability and vortex flowmeter selection.

image.alt: Industrial pipeline installed close to large pump motors

cardDescription: Pump, compressor and process lines where vibration affects signal stability.
whereItFits: Vibration-prone lines appear near pumps, compressors, reducers and weak pipe supports.
siteCondition: Vibration-prone process lines can appear near pumps, compressors, reducers and unstable pipe supports.
challenge: Mechanical vibration can affect signal quality and make installation details more important than a model number.

metadata.title: Flow Measurement for High-Vibration Pipelines | Velomac
metadata.description: Review flow measurement near pumps, compressors and unstable pipe supports where mechanical vibration can interfere with signal stability.

detailPage.introduction: Vibration source, pipe support, flow range and meter position should be reviewed together before selecting a meter for a vibration-prone line.
detailPage.measurementTitle: Separate process flow from mechanical vibration
detailPage.measurementText: Document the vibration source and pipe layout along with the media and operating range so signal stability and installation limits can be reviewed.

title: Energy Loss Visibility
focus: Flow measurement as a way to locate hidden energy waste in steam, compressed air, cooling water and process utilities.

image.alt: Industrial steam pipeline with visible leakage near a flowmeter

cardDescription: Utility flow measurement for steam, compressed air, cooling water and process lines.
whereItFits: Utility networks can lose energy through leaks, bypasses and poorly monitored use points.
siteCondition: Utility networks often lose energy through leaks, bypasses, oversized lines or poorly monitored usage points.
challenge: Without measured flow, operators may see energy cost but not know which line or process is responsible.

metadata.title: Industrial Utility & Energy Flow Visibility | Velomac
metadata.description: Plan flow measurement points for steam, compressed air, cooling water and process utilities to make usage and potential losses more visible.

detailPage.h1: Industrial Utility and Energy Flow Visibility
detailPage.introduction: Useful utility measurement starts by defining which line, user or process needs to become visible and how the resulting flow data will be used.
detailPage.measurementTitle: Define the utility boundary and metering point
detailPage.measurementText: Identify the utility, expected operating range, measurement location and data output before selecting the meter technology.
